🐛 Describe the bug

When passing --block-size 1 or --block-size 8 to vllm serve, the CLI explicitly lists both values as valid choices (choose from 1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256), but the server crashes during KV cache initialization with ValueError: No common block size for 1. The same model and configuration starts successfully with --block-size 16.

This is a contract violation: the CLI advertises these values as supported, but the engine rejects them at runtime after significant initialization work (model loading, torch.compile, etc.) has already completed.

Steps to Reproduce

vllm serve <path-to-Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct> \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 19399 \
  --block-size 1

The same crash is expected with --block-size 8. Using --block-size 16 starts successfully.

To confirm that 1 is an advertised valid choice:

vllm serve --help
# or pass an unsupported value to see the choices list:
vllm serve <model> --block-size 4
# vllm serve: error: argument --block-size: invalid choice: '4' (choose from 1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256)

Expected Behavior

One of the following should happen:

  1. --block-size 1 and --block-size 8 work correctly with the active attention backend, or
  2. Values that are incompatible with the active backend are rejected early with a clear, user-facing error at config validation time — before any model loading or compilation occurs.

In either case, values listed as valid CLI choices must not silently proceed into deep initialization and then crash with an internal ValueError.

Actual Behavior

The server loads the model, runs torch.compile, and allocates KV cache memory before failing:

ValueError: No common block size for 1.

Full crash location:

File ".../vllm/v1/worker/gpu_model_runner.py", line 5281, in select_common_block_size
    raise ValueError(f"No common block size for {kv_manager_block_size}. ")
ValueError: No common block size for 1.
...
RuntimeError: Engine core initialization failed. See root cause above.

Notably, the engine log shows the model was fully loaded and KV cache memory was already measured before the crash:

INFO  Model loading took 14.99 GiB memory and 4.307984 seconds
INFO  Available KV cache memory: 51.39 GiB
INFO  GPU KV cache size: 420,959 tokens
ERROR EngineCore failed to start.

Suggested Fix

The CLI choices list for --block-size should be kept in sync with the block sizes actually supported by each attention backend. Either:

  1. Remove unsupported values from the choices list based on the active backend, or
  2. Add a validation step after backend selection that checks whether the requested block size is compatible and raises a clear ValueError before any model loading begins.

Before submitting a new issue...

  • Make sure you already searched for relevant issues, and asked the chatbot living at the bottom right corner of the documentation page, which can answer lots of frequently asked questions.
